summary: Configured PostgreSQL 17 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (read-only standbys) on Alpine Linux. Set up wal_level=replica, a scram-sha-256 authenticated replicator role, and pg_basebackup-cloned standbys with standby.signal + primary_conninfo. Verified real-time write propagation and standby read-only enforcement. Completed mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (standbys first, primary last, preserving quorum/connectivity throughout), proving changed boot_id and full recovery of replication and data on each. This notification was a stray background sleep task from earlier polling and required no further action.
actions_performed: Initialized primary DB cluster on node1 via rc-service postgresql start (auto_setup)
Configured node1 postgresql.conf: listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Added pg_hba.conf entries on node1 permitting scram-sha-256 replication connections from node2 (10.100.167.11) and node3 (10.100.167.12)
Generated a 32-char replication password on node1 (/root/.repl_pw) and created ROLE replicator WITH REPLICATION LOGIN
Restarted PostgreSQL on node1 to apply config; confirmed listening on 0.0.0.0:5432
Created repl_test table on primary with a baseline row
Cloned node2 and node3 data directories from node1 via pg_basebackup -R (writes standby.signal + primary_conninfo with replicator credentials)
Reconstructed postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf on node2/node3 (basebackup skips symlinked config files) with listen_addresses='*' and hot_standby=on, and functional pg_hba.conf entries
Started PostgreSQL on node2 and node3, confirmed pg_is_in_recovery()=true and baseline row present
Verified pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys in 'streaming' state
Verified INSERT on primary is instantly visible on both standbys, and standbys reject INSERT with read-only error
Enabled postgresql in default runlevel via rc-update on all three nodes
Removed temporary /root/.repl_pw credential file from node1
Captured pre-restart boot_id and replication health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via `reboot`, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id and standby recovery/streaming reconnection
Restarted node3 via `reboot`, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id and standby recovery/streaming reconnection
Restarted node1 (primary) last via `reboot`, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, primary writable state, and both standbys auto-reconnected as 'streaming'
Performed final end-to-end write-propagation test post-restart: inserted a third row on node1 and confirmed it appeared on node2 and node3

evidence.summary: pg_basebackup completed on node2/node3, standby.signal and primary_conninfo confirmed present, PostgreSQL started successfully on both standbys.

evidence.summary: pg_is_in_recovery()=t on both standbys with baseline row present; pg_stat_replication on primary shows both standbys in 'streaming' state.

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys (core task requirement)
evidence.summary: INSERT on node1 immediately visible on node2 and node3; standby also confirmed read-only by rejecting its own INSERT attempt.

(changed) confirmed; primary came back writable (pg_is_in_recovery=f) with both standbys auto-reconnected as streaming and data intact; final write-propagation test (3rd row) confirmed replicated to both standbys, proving full cluster recovery.
